See what data NDC Shelf handles, where it connects, its sources, licenses, and how to get in touch.
There are no accounts, no ads, and no developer-run analytics, crash reporting, or sync servers. Browsing and editing your library works offline. Connections to outside services are listed below.

Barcode recognition runs on the device with an ML Kit model. ISBNs, bibliographic data, NDC codes, reading status, locations, and purchase plans are stored in an on-device Room database and are never sent to the developer\'s servers. Continuous scan history keeps only ISBNs and results, for the most recent 20 sessions.

When you look up an ISBN, only that ISBN is sent to NDL Search over HTTPS. Only if you explicitly enable scheduled series checks, the series name and the search start year are sent once a week per series. After a temporary failure, only the failed check is retried with exponential backoff. Your library, reading status, locations, and purchase plans are never sent. Covers are fetched only from that same service and cached up to 50 MiB. Each destination receives ordinary connection details such as your IP address. ML Kit does not send what it recognizes to Google, but it does send diagnostic and usage information. All traffic is encrypted with HTTPS.

All data is excluded from Android cloud backup. On Android 9 and later, only the Room database is included in device-to-device transfer; on Android 8.1 and earlier, OS-level transfer is excluded as well. JSON, CSV, and full backups are written only to the destination you choose, and the app never uploads them on its own. A full backup also contains purchase plans and scan history. These files are not encrypted, so the destination needs its own protection.
This app uses the NDL Search API. Some bibliographic data and NDC codes originate from that service and from each contributing metadata provider; the content and terms of use differ by provider.
